title: Salman Khan Apologises to Shraddha Kapoor Over December 4 Box-Office Clash
excerpt: His Maatrubhumi and her Eetha open on the same Friday, December 4, 2026. Salman says he did not know her date when his was announced, called her to say sorry — and told audiences to watch her film.
body:
• Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace and Shraddha Kapoor's Eetha are both scheduled to open in cinemas on Friday, December 4, 2026.
  • Salman says he did not know Eetha held the date when his team announced Maatrubhumi for December 4 — and that he called Shraddha Kapoor personally to apologise.
  • According to Salman, Shraddha told him there is enough space for both films; he responded by urging audiences to go and watch Eetha.
  • Both are Hindi films, but very different ones: Maatrubhumi is Apoorva Lakhia's patriotic drama with Chitrangada Singh, while Eetha is Laxman Utekar's biopic of Lavani legend Vithabai Bhau Mang Narayangaonkar.

Salman Khan has apologised to Shraddha Kapoor after his film Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace was set for a December 4, 2026 theatrical release — the same Friday as her biopic Eetha. Speaking at an event with ABP News, the actor said the clash was unintentional, and that he telephoned Shraddha himself once he learned her film was arriving on the same date, according to Bollywood Hungama.

"So, when we announced the 4th (of December), I did not know that Shraddha was coming out on the 4th of December. I feel really, really bad about it. If I would've known, I would not have come out with Shraddha."

— Salman Khan, at an ABP News event

The phone call

Salman said he has watched Shraddha and her family grow up in the industry, which made the overlap harder to leave unaddressed. "I spoke to her. I called her up. I mean, I've seen them grow up. I spoke to her and said, 'I'm really sorry, I didn't know,'" he recalled. Her answer, by his account, settled the matter: "But she said, 'No, no, sir. There's enough space for both of our films to come'. So I told her, 'Very good, I'm happy'." He went further in public, adding of Eetha: "I do think that everyone should go and see that film." Box Office Worldwide carried the same account of the exchange.

Two very different films, one Friday

Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace is a Hindi patriotic drama directed by Apoorva Lakhia, featuring Salman alongside Chitrangada Singh, combining emotional and action elements. Eetha is a Hindi biographical drama directed by Laxman Utekar and backed by Maddock Films, in which Shraddha Kapoor plays Vithabai Bhau Mang Narayangaonkar, the celebrated Tamasha and Lavani exponent; the film also features Randeep Hooda and Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub.

The two films are not chasing the same opening-weekend audience in the same way — a star-led war drama and a music-rooted biopic sell different evenings out — which is the practical basis for Shraddha's "enough space" response. Neither production has announced a change of date, so as things stand both films open on Friday, December 4, 2026, in Indian cinemas, with overseas releases in markets including the US expected the same weekend; exhibitors in those markets will confirm screens closer to the date.

What to watch for

Release-date clashes are usually fought through screen counts and distribution deals, not phone calls, which is why this one has drawn attention. The next markers are practical: whether either studio adjusts its date in the final weeks, and how exhibitors split screens between the two titles when advance bookings open. For now, both films keep December 4 — and the bigger star in the clash has publicly told his audience to watch the other film too.
